title.narrative: Ghana - Pre-financing shea production of smallholder farmers

description.narrative: With a DGGF loan Sommalife Impact Group B.V. will be able to support shea nut smallholder farmers in Northern Ghana with pre-finance.Sommalife aims to disburse funds early in the season (april-june) in order to support the farmers in bridging the gap of the low-season. During this low-season these farmers often run out of money which leads to a stronger need to search for additional income. One quick way of earning money is to cut down trees and sell it as charcoal. Ghana has already lost more than 20% of its original forestation and poverty is one of the contributing problems. Crucial results to make this project successful is early disbursement of funds to reduce poverty in early stages. A second good result is the recovery rate where Sommalife looks at how much of the disbursed funds they can recover from the farmers. As Sommalife does all the sourcing itself, they are not dependent on third party suppliers. To deliver their goods to the port and receive customer payments, third party truck transport is needed to deliver the goods. After the goods have been delivered and the customer has paid, the project can be seen as successful and does not require any additional funding to remain the impact. Apart from a lower need to cut trees for charcoal income, the project has other positive development effects like education on the value of trees and local employment. During the pre financing period, the farmers are trained and educated on the value of their trees and how cutting those trees will only worsen their longer-term income. The pre-financing period requires extra employment from Sommalife staff as staff members operational in the field, field agents, are required to return to the field extra times for education on pre-financing, disbursing the funds and recovering the funds.
